 JUDGMENT

This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,50,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

2. Briefly stated, the case of the petitioner is as follows:
That on 07.06.2020 at about 5.30 p.m., when the petitioner was standing after finishing his coolie work, the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA- 06-TB-4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 which belongs to Krishnappa drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

He took treatment in Government Hospital, Tumkur and Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre,
Tumkur .

entities.text:
Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre,
Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: A case was registered in Crime No.91/2020 against the driver of the tractor and trailer at Hebbur police station.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to appear before the Court and he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its advocate and filed written statement by denying the petition averments as false.
The first respondent has not complied with the mandatory requirements of Section 134(c) of M.V.Act and Police have not complied the mandatory requirements of Section 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties such as driver of the tractor and trailer who was not made as party to the proceedings.

The tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB-4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 was insured with it with commercial vehicle package policy No.MA404781 for the period from 01.10.2019 to 30.09.2020 and the accident has occurred on 17.06.2020.
At the time of accident there was no F.C. for the tractor and trailer and it amounts to violation of conditions of the policy.
As per the police documents, the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of the petitioner as he was standing on the mud portion area without observing the moving tractor.

The driver of the tractor and trailer had no driving licence to drive the same on the date of accident and the owner knowingly fully well that driver had no driving licence has entrusted the vehicle to him and has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.

The complaint was lodged 17.06.2020 before the jurisdictional police and Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84784414/
2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: there is delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint and there are no proper reasons assigned for the delay in lodging the complaint.
As per wound certificate accident date is mentioned as 08.06.2020 and as per FIR accident occurred on 07.06.2020.
The jurisdictional police by colluding with the claimant have filed a false case against the respondent to make wrongful gain.
The compensation claimed is unrelated and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of of tractor and trailer bearing reg.
No.KA-06-TB-4971 and KA-06-TB-4972 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was standing and working as a coolie in the above said Tractor and trailer and he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.06.2020?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred due to negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself?
3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order?
5. On behalf of the petitioner, he examined himself as PW-1 and two witnesses are examined as PWs 2 and 3 and got marked Exhibits P.1 to P.19.
The respondent No.2 has examined one witness as RW-1 and got marked two documents at Exs.R.1 and R.2.

6. Heard the arguments of both sides.
7.

My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1 ... In the Affirmative, Issue No.2 ... Partly in affirmative, awarding compensation of Rs.6,81,400/ - from the respondents Issue No.3 ...

As per final order for the following:-
REASONS 8. Issues No.1 and 2:
Since these issues involve common discussion, I have taken them together.

The petitioner in order to prove this issue has placed reliance on his oral evidence and documentary evidence as per Exs.P.1 to P.7 and P.16 such as FIR with complaint, wound certificate, spot mahazar,
notice issued under Section 133 of MV Act, reply to notice, IMV report, charge sheet and MLC extract.

PW-1 being the petitioner and the injured, in his affidavit evidence has narrated how he met with an accident and the accident was due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the tractor and Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs.,

The first respondent being the son of the owner of the said tractor has remained exparte.

The second respondent being the insurer in the written statement has contended that there is delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint and there are no proper reasons assigned for the delay and as such jurisdictional police by colluding with the petitioner has registered a false case and the alleged accident occurred mainly due to the negligence of the petitioner as he was standing on the mud proration area without observing the moving tractor,as such there is 100% negligence of the petitioner.
The second respondent has examined the Public Relation Officer of Shidlaghatta Medical College Hospital, Tumkur as RW-1 and RW1 has produced MLC Extract as per Ex.R.2.

Ex.P.16 and Ex.R.2 are one and the same.
9.

As per PW-1 on 07.06.2020 at about 5.30 P.M. when he was working as a coolie under the first respondent in a tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB- 4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 on Buchanahalli lake, Gulur Hobli, Tumkur taluk, at that time the driver of the tractor has driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner causing the accident and thereby petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

The mother of the petitioner has lodged the complaint on 17.06.2020 to the police and on the basis of the said complaint, the police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB- 4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972.
Thus, there is delay of 10 days in lodging the complaint.

In the complaint the mother of the petitioner has stated that immediately after the accident her son was admitted to Government hospital, Tumkur and then he was brought back to the house, but as the condition of the petitioner was not good, on the next day i.e., on 08.06.2020,
the petitioner was shifted to Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur, wherein he took treatment for accidental injuries and except her as there were nobody to look after her son, she was with her son providing treatment to him and as such there was delay in lodging the complaint.
10. PW-1 was cross-examined by the second respondent counsel on this aspect.

sentences.text: Thus, the complaint and the evidence of PW1 reveals the reason for delay in lodging the complaint.

Merely because there was delay in lodging the complaint, the claim of the petitioner cannot be doubted when the mother of the petitioner has given prime importance in treating the petitioner rather than lodging the complaint.

In MLC Extract- Ex.P.16 and in Ex.R.2, it is clearly mentioned that the petitioner was admitted to Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre,
Tumkur on 08.06.2020 with the history of accident in view of tractor hitting him from the front and he was got under the tractor tyre.

sentences.text: When MLC extract clearly discloses that the petitioner was admitted to Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur with the history of accident through a tractor , it cannot be said that the jurisdictional police by colluding with the petitioner has registered a false case against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: As such explanation assigned by the complainant and the petitioner for delay in lodging the complaint has to be accepted as a plausible explanation.
11. Ex.P.3 is the spot mahazar drawn by the police at the accident spot.

In Ex.P.3 it is mentioned that accident took place when the petitioner was standing in the middle of tank portion of Buchanahalli village where mud was filled and that place is situated about 20-25 feet away from the tank bund Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84784414/
4
and it was with a depth of about 3 to 4 feet and it was a ditch measuring 15"x15" length and the breadth .
As per PW1 in his cross-examination on the date of accident he had been to do coolie work in the tractor and trailer belonging to the first respondent.

The contents of the complaint discloses that on that day after dumping the mud in the tractor , when the petitioner was standing infront of the tractor, tractor has dashed to the petitioner resulting in accident.
As such, the contents mentioned in Ex.P.3 clearly establishes that accident occurred when the petitioner was standing infront of the tractor after dumping the mud to the tractor.
12. Exhibits P.4 and P.5 are the notices issued to the owner of the tractor and the reply given by him.

In Ex.P.5, the son of the owner of the tractor has categorically stated that at the time of accident one Dadha Jan was the driver of the tractor and it was taken by him to dump mud near the house of Srinivasa and the petitioner had been to the said place as a coolie to dump the mud in the tractor and the petitioner sustained injuries on account of tractor hitting him from front side.
These documents also supports the case of the petitioner.
13. Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report which discloses that no damages were found on the tractor and trailer.
Ex.P.2 - wound certificate which discloses that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries in the accident.

During the course of cross-examination of PW1, a suggestion was made that accident has occurred due to his negligence as he was sitting on the mudguard of the tractor and as the tractor moved with speed, he fell down from the tractor.
This suggestion was denied by PW1.
Except making the suggestion to PW1 , the second respondent has not chosen to summon the driver of the tractor to prove its contention.

In the absence of any evidence on the part of the second respondent,
the suggestions made to PW1 are of no consequence.
14. Ex.P.7 is the chargesheet filed by the police against the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB-4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 after detailed investigation.
This chargesheet was not challenged by the driver of the tractor.
The conduct of the driver of the tractor in not challenging the chargesheet itself is sufficient to hold that as the accident took place due to his negligence, he remained silent.

By considering all these aspects and the evidence placed on record, I am of the opinion that the petitioner has proved that he has sustained injuries in an accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent act on the part of the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB-4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 , whereas the second respondent has failed to prove that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative and issue No.2 in the negative.

15. ISSUE No.3:
(a). Pain and Agony:
PW-1 has produced the wound Certificate at Ex.P.2 which discloses that the petitioner has sustained (1) right iliac blade fracture, right sacroiliac joint fracture dislocation, fracture of the bilateral superior and inferior pubic ramus fracture, focal liver contusion with hemoperitoneum , raw wound over the right dorsal aspect of the right thigh .
X-ray shows Iliac blade fracture, right joint fracture dislocation .

As per Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84784414/

Discharge summary-

Ex.P.9 and case sheet Ex.P.18 discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment in Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur from 08.06.2020 to 15.06.2020 and he has undergone surgery by open reduction and internal fixation and also skin grafting for the accidental injuries.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Follow up sheets of Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur as per Ex.P.14 and X-ray at Ex.P.15 confirms the sustaining of the injuries by the petitioner as mentioned in the wound certificate.

entities.text: Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The injuries sustained by the petitioner requires minimum 5 months treatment.
During the treatment period, the petitioner has suffered lot of pain and agony.

So, taking into account the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and number of days of his treatment in the hospital, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under the head Pain and agony.

(b). Medical Expenses (including conveyance, attendant charges and extra nourishment):
PW-1 has deposed that, he has spent more than Rs.2,50,000/- towards medicines and treatment, Rs.45,500/- towards attendant charges and nourishment and Rs.55,500/- towards car rentals for his follow up treatment.

In support of his evidence PW1 has produced medical bills and prescriptions as per Exs.P.10 and P.11.
Ex.P.10 are amounting to Rs.87,877/-.
The petitioner is entitled for the amount claimed under Ex.P.10(1) towards acetabulam instrumentation charges.
The other medical bills of Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur are with respect to lab charges, consultation, C.T.Scan , MRI etc.,

entities.text: Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled for the amount claimed under the bills of Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur .

entities.text: Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The other bills are pharmacy bills which do not contain the signature of the person who has issued them and seal of the shop.
As such, it cannot be said that the petitioner has spent the amount claimed under those pharmacy bills for his treatment.
The petitioner has not produced conveyance bills, except claiming that he has spent Rs.55,500/- towards car rentals,

However, by considering the nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and the type of treatment undergone by the petitioner, it can be said that the petitioner has spent some amount towards medicines, nourishment and attendant charges.

Hence, I deem it just and proper to award compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.
(c) Loss of income during the treatment period:
PW-1 has deposed that, at the time of accident he was working as a coolie by loading and unloading in the tractor and trailer of respondent No.1 and he was earning a sum of Rs.20,000/-.p.m., but due to the accident he is not in a position to do any work and he has lost his income.
Except the oral assertion of PW1, no materials are produced in proof of his avocation and income.

In the absence of any materials before the Court, the income of the petitioner as fixed under the Minimum Wages Act has to be taken in view of the judgment of the Division Bench of our own High Court in MFA No.7404/2014 (Smt.Mariyamma and others Vs Sri Suyambulingam and Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84784414/
6 another), dated 06.12.2022.

entities.text: Smt.Mariyamma and others Vs Sri Suyambulingam and Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This accident has occurred in the year 2020.

As per the Minimum Wages Act, the income of the petitioner has to be taken at Rs.11,000/p.m.
Injuries sustained by the petitioner require minimum 5 months treatment.
During that period petitioner was unable to do any work.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.55,000/- under this head.
(d) Future loss of earning capacity:

PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is not in a position to do any work and he cannot stand for long time, lift weight, climb stair case, he suffers from severe headache which has badly affected his profession and he has suffered permanent disability.
In order to prove the disability, the petitioner has examined the Doctor as PW3.
PW3 has deposed that the petitioner suffers from total physical disability of right lower limb at 67% and whole body disability at 23%.
Whether the disability assessed by PW3 is to be accepted or not has to be scrutinized cautiously.
PW-3 in his cross-examination
has deposed that he has not treated the petitioner personally, but he has assessed the disability based on wound certificate and discharge summary .
As per PW3 surgery was conducted to the fracture of pelvic bone.
It was suggested to PW3 that as he has not treated the petitioner, he is not competent to assess the disability.
PW3 has denied the said suggestion.

Merely because PW3 has not treated the petitioner, his evidence cannot be brushed aside,
when he being an orthopaedic surgeon, is also competent to assess the disability.

On perusal of the cross-examination of PW3, it is noticed that the second respondent has disputed only the percentage of disability given by PW3 by suggesting that he has assessed the disability on higher side.
Admittedly, the petitioner is a coolie.
As such it can be safely held that the disability stated by PW3 will definitely reduce the earning capacity of the petitioner to some extent.
By considering the avocation of the petitioner as coolie, the functional disability is taken at 15% .
The income of the petitioner is taken at Rs.11,000/p.m.
The annual income of the petitioner comes to Rs.1,32,000/-.
According to the petitioner he was aged 20 years at the time of accident.
PW-1 has produced his Aadhar Card as per Ex.P.8, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 06.04.2001.
Accident occurred on 07.06.2020.
Hence, by considering the said date of birth of the petitioner, it can be said that the petitioner was aged 19 years as on the date of accident.
Depending upon the said age, as per the ratio laid down in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 (Sarala Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation) the proper multiplier applicable is 18.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So loss of future income comes to Rs.3,56,400/-.
As such, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.3,56,400/- under this head.

(e) Future Medical Expenses:

sentences.text: 7 PW-1 has deposed that, he has to undergo another surgery for removal of implants and the cost of said surgery is around Rs.60,000/-.
PW3 in his cross- examination has deposed that he has not given any estimation to show that the petitioner requires Rs.60,000/- for further surgery.
The medical records disclose that the petitioner has undergone surgery by fixation of implants and as such they have to be removed.
Hence, by considering that the petitioner requires some amount towards future medical expenses, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.30,000/- under this head.
(f) Towards unhappiness and loss of amenities:

PW-1 has deposed that due to the accidental injuries, he is not in a position to do any work and he cannot stand for long time, lift weight, climb stair case, he suffers from severe headache which has badly affected his profession and he has suffered permanent disability.

PW3 has deposed that the petitioner is unable to walk normally, unable to sit down, lift weights and carry his job as coolie and there is a scar over right thigh, restricted right hip and right lower limb muscles, reduced pelvic girth and the petitioner suffers from total physical disability of right lower limb at 67% and to the whole body physical disability at 23%.
Hence, from the difficulties stated by PWs 1 and 2, it can be said that the petitioner suffered from unhappiness and discomfort while doing his normal activities and avocation.
Hence, I deem it just and proper to award Rs.80,000/- under this head.

16. In view of the reasons stated above, in all the petitioner is entitled to the compensation as under:
Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No.
a. Pain and Agony Rs. 60,000-00 b.

Medical Expenses (conveyance, Rs. 1,00,000-00  nourishment and attendant  charges)
c. Loss of income during the Rs. 55,000-00  treatment and rest period d. Loss of future income due to Rs. 3,56,400-00  disability e.
Future medical expenses Rs. 30,000-00 f. Unhappiness and loss of Rs. 80,000-00  amenities in life  TOTAL Rs. 6,81,400-00
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.6,81,400/- with interest on Rs.6,51,000/- at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.

sentences.text: So far as the liability is concerned, according to the petitioner, the first respondent is the son of the owner of the tractor and trailer in question and the second respondent is the insurer of the said vehicle.

Respondent No.2 in his written statement has admitted that it has issued the policy in favour of the insured with respect to the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB- 4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 for the period from 01.10.2019 to 30.09.2020.
Accident occurred on 07.06.2020, hence, the policy was valid as on the date of accident.

As such, I am of the opinion that the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.6,81,400/-
to the petitioner along with interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.6,51,000/- from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.

18. Issue No.4 : In view of my findings on the above said issues and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER

The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.6,81,400/- (Rupees six lakhs eighty one thousand four hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., on Rs.6,51,000/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation of Rs.15,50,000/- along with interest from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
Due to the impact he fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
He took treatment in Government Hospital, Tumkur and Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre,
Tumkur .
A case was registered in Crime No.91/2020 against the driver of the tractor and trailer at Hebbur police station.
Hence, this petition for compensation.
3. In response to the notice of the petition, the respondent No.1 has not chosen to appear before the Court and he was placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the Court through its advocate and filed written statement by denying the petition averments as false.
The first respondent has not complied with the mandatory requirements of Section 134(c) of M.V.Act and Police have not complied the mandatory requirements of Section 158(6) of M.V.Act.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties such as driver of the tractor and trailer who was not made as party to the proceedings.
The tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB-4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972 was insured with it with commercial vehicle package policy No.MA404781 for the period from 01.10.2019 to 30.09.2020 and the accident has occurred on 17.06.2020.
At the time of accident there was no F.C. for the tractor and trailer and it amounts to violation of conditions of the policy.
As per the police documents, the alleged accident was occurred mainly due to the negligence of the petitioner as he was standing on the mud portion area without observing the moving tractor.
The driver of the tractor and trailer had no driving licence to drive the same on the date of accident and the owner knowingly fully well that driver had no driving licence has entrusted the vehicle to him and has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
The complaint was lodged 17.06.2020 before the jurisdictional police and Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84784414/
2
The jurisdictional police by colluding with the claimant have filed a false case against the respondent to make wrongful gain.
The compensation claimed is unrelated and exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that due to rash and negligent driving of of tractor and trailer bearing reg.
No.KA-06-TB-4971 and KA-06-TB-4972 by its driver dashed to the petitioner who was standing and working as a coolie in the above said Tractor and trailer and he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.06.2020?
2. Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the accident has occurred due to negligent act on the part of the petitioner himself?
3.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?
If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
4.
What order?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The mother of the petitioner has lodged the complaint on 17.06.2020 to the police and on the basis of the said complaint, the police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the tractor and trailer bearing registration No.KA-06-TB- 4971 and No.KA-06-TB-4972.
Merely because there was delay in lodging the complaint, the claim of the petitioner cannot be doubted when the mother of the petitioner has given prime importance in treating the petitioner rather than lodging the complaint.
When MLC extract clearly discloses that the petitioner was admitted to Siddhartha Medical College and Research Centre, Tumkur with the history of accident through a tractor , it cannot be said that the jurisdictional police by colluding with the petitioner has registered a false case against the driver of the Tractor and Trailer.
As such explanation assigned by the complainant and the petitioner for delay in lodging the complaint has to be accepted as a plausible explanation.
This chargesheet was not challenged by the driver of the tractor.
In the absence of any materials before the Court, the income of the petitioner as fixed under the Minimum Wages Act has to be taken in view of the judgment of the Division Bench of our own High Court in MFA No.7404/2014 (Smt.Mariyamma and others Vs Sri Suyambulingam and Rakshith B.G vs Lakshmamma Dead Lrs., By Krishnappa on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84784414/
6 another), dated 06.12.2022.
As per the Minimum Wages Act, the income of the petitioner has to be taken at Rs.11,000/p.m.
Injuries sustained by the petitioner require minimum 5 months treatment.
Merely because PW3 has not treated the petitioner, his evidence cannot be brushed aside,
when he being an orthopaedic surgeon, is also competent to assess the disability.

Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.6,81,400/- with interest on Rs.6,51,000/- at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.
As such, I am of the opinion that the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation of Rs.6,81,400/-
to the petitioner along with interest at 6% p.a. on Rs.6,51,000/- from the date of the petition till deposit in Court.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.
18. Issue No.4 : In view of my findings on the above said issues and for the reasons stated therein , I proceed to pass the following: -
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner is allowed in part with costs against the respondents No.1 and 2, awarding compensation of Rs.6,81,400/- (Rupees six lakhs eighty one thousand four hundred only) with interest at 6% p.a., on Rs.6,51,000/- from the date of petition till the date of deposit in Court.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
However, the respondent No.2, being the Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount in Court within 3 months from the date of this order.
After deposit of the compensation amount, 50% with proportionate interest shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any of the nationalized or scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Remaining 50% with proportionate interest is ordered to be released to the petitioner.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/- .
Draw an Award accordingly.
